title: Dynamic SKU burn-rate and contingency planning
content:
Purpose:
Quick-reference capacity planning sheet that ties SKU-specific burn rates to dynamic reorder triggers and contingency lanes across regions. Intended as an operational runbook for infra/planning to use when lead times shift or demand surges.

Executive summary:
- We currently operate three contingency lanes (Primary, Secondary, Emergency) for GPU delivery. This sheet introduces a dynamic reorder-point formula that incorporates measured burn-rate volatility, lead-time variance, and committed customer capacity.
- Recommendation: move from fixed-days safety stock to a volatility-weighted safety buffer and a small central floating pool (5% of total fleet) for cross-region emergency swaps.

Assumptions (for calculations below):
- Demand window used: trailing 90 days, smoothed with exponential decay (alpha=0.2).
- Lead-time is order-to-availability at datacenter (not transit). Use vendor-reported median + vendor volatility factor.
- Committed capacity = Dedicated + Reserved customer capacity from contracts.
- Burn = average GPU-hours consumed per SKU, converted to a monthly equivalent.

Current snapshot (as of 2024-11-12):
Region,SKU,QtyAvailable,QtyCommitted,QtyReserve(safety),LeadTimeMedianDays,LeadTimeStdDays,MonthlyBurnEstimate
us-west-1,A100-80GB,420,280,30,45,8,320
us-west-1,H100-80GB,120,70,20,70,12,95
eu-west-1,A100-80GB,210,150,20,50,10,160
eu-west-1,H100-80GB,80,40,10,80,18,70
apac-southeast-1,A100-80GB,90,40,10,60,14,60
apac-southeast-1,H100-80GB,30,20,5,90,25,25
central-floating-pool (unallocated),mixed,60,0,60,NA,NA,NA

Notes on snapshot:
- Central floating pool (60 GPUs) is intentionally small to avoid idle hardware cost; used for emergency swaps and inter-region trial bursts.
- H100 lead times show larger variance; treat H100 as higher procurement risk.

Dynamic reorder point (DRP) formula (stringent):
DRP = ceil( (MonthlyBurn * LeadTimeDays/30) + (z * sqrt(LeadTimeDays/30) * VolatilityFactor * MonthlyBurn) + CommittedDelta )
Where:
- z = 1.645 (95th percentile one-sided) for high-confidence restock
- VolatilityFactor = max(0.15, LeadTimeStdDays / LeadTimeMedianDays) (floors at 15%)
- CommittedDelta = additional buffer for signed contracts not yet delivered (in GPU units)

Example calculation (us-west-1 H100):
- MonthlyBurn = 95 GPUs
- LeadTimeDays = 70 -> LeadTimeDays/30 = 2.33 months
- LeadTimeStdDays = 12 -> VolatilityFactor = max(0.15, 12/70 = 0.171) -> 0.171
- DRP base = 95 * 2.33 = 221.35 -> round up 222
- Volatility buffer = 1.645 * sqrt(2.33) * 0.171 * 95 = ~1.645*1.53*0.171*95 ~= 41
- If CommittedDelta = 15 (new reserved deals), DRP = 222 + 41 + 15 = 278 GPUs

Interpretation: us-west-1 needs ~278 H100 capacity to hit 95% safe restock confidence with current burn/variance and commitments. Current available+reserve (120+20) = 140 -> reorder quantity ~138 (or pursue swaps/fallbacks).

Contingency lanes (operational definitions):
- Primary: normal replenishment schedule via long-lead vendor contracts (targeted at median lead time).
- Secondary: expedite orders / alternative vendors / regional transfers (cost premium).
- Emergency: central floating pool + cross-region swap + rental partners (short-term).

Procurement cadence recommendations:
- Weekly pipeline cadence meeting: review open POs, expected deliveries 0-90 days, and compare to DRP heatmap.
- Monthly SKU reforecast: run DRP across all region/SKU rows; flag any SKU with shortfall > 25% of DRP.
- Quarterly capacity review: re-evaluate volatility floors and z-level (can lower to 1.28 for business-critical cost-saving experiments).

Swap and fallback playbook (when reorder delta > available):
1) If reorder quantity > 80% of vendor MOQ or budget requires phasing, trigger A/B fallback: consider serving H100-backed workloads on A100 quantized variants with expected quality regression notes (see linked artifacts).
2) Evaluate cross-region swap: move GPUs from region with >= 20% spare-to-DRP to region with deficit. Document network egress costs and transit lead time.
3) Place staggered expedited order (Secondary lane) for remaining deficit, gain ETA and update customers.
4) If still short, allocate from central floating pool and start emergency rental vendor outreach.

Cost and procurement tradeoffs (high-level):
- Example: Expedited H100 order cost premium ~ +18% vs standard. Rental short-term spot can be +40–150%/month. Quantization/variant fallback could reduce HW needs by ~30% but carries model quality risk.
- Recommendation: Reserve expedited lane for H100 deficits above 50 GPUs or when SLA impact > 5% of customer spend.

Operational metrics to track (sheet columns recommended):
- ETA (vendor), PO id, SKU, Qty ordered, Qty received, Region, Intended pool (hosted/dedicated/private), Commitments impacted (customer ids), Days to fulfill, Cost premium %, Source (primary/secondary/emergency), Notes.

Decision log (recent):
- 2024-10-22: Agreed to create central floating pool (60 GPUs) after pilot showed 14% fewer late SLAs. (Decision: Ethan Chen)
- 2024-11-01: Volatility floor set to 15% to avoid overreacting to short-term spikes. (Decision: Maya Patel)
- 2024-12-10: Lowered z from 1.96 to 1.645 for DRP to balance cost/availability on non-critical SKUs. (Action pending finance signoff)

Risks and actions:
- Vendor concentration risk: two main H100 vendors account for 85% of capacity -> onboard one additional supplier (RFP initiated JIRA-INFRA-889).
- Lead time reporting mismatch: vendors report transit + install differently; standardize to 'order -> datacenter-ready' metric (owner: Alex Gomez).

Immediate next steps (first 14 days):
- Run full DRP for all SKU-region combos and produce a shortfall heatmap (owner: Ethan) by 2024-11-20.
- Initiate expedited quote request for H100 (us-west-1) to cover ~120 GPUs shortfall (owner: Maya) - include rental partners if vendor cannot meet target ETA.
- Update procurement SOP to include DRP calculation and gate for expedited lane approvals (owner: Ravi).

Appendix: quick reference calculation snippets (copy to automation):
- VolatilityFactor = max(0.15, lead_time_std / lead_time_median)
- months_in_lead = lead_time_days / 30.0
- drp = ceil(months_in_lead * monthly_burn + z * sqrt(months_in_lead) * volatility_factor * monthly_burn + committed_delta)

Questions / open items:
- Should we treat transit lead times separately for APAC given frequent customs delays? (open, owner: Alex)
- Do we want an automated alert when DRP shortfall hits 10% of monthly burn for any SKU? (ops request ticketed)

Contact / owners: Ethan Chen (ethan@redwood.ai), Maya Patel (maya@redwood.ai), Ravi Subramanian (ravi@redwood.ai), Alex Gomez (alex@redwood.ai)

This doc is intentionally operational and spreadsheet-first; copy DRP formulas into procurement automation toy scripts and integrate into the weekly pipeline dashboard.
